findings.message: The notebook's pipeline cell calls `wg_fin.load_artifacts` and `wg_fin.run_inference`, but `financial_impact/financial.py` defines neither, so the cell fails on every run and never produces the reports it exists to make. financial.py defines only merge_predictions, decode_labels, build_batch_df, decompose, get_params, compute_financials and save_reports, and its docstring says it is 'Fully decoupled from inference and artifact loading'. Trace: notebook line 185 `artifacts = wg_fin.load_artifacts(artifact_dir)` raises AttributeError. The broad `except Exception as e:` catches it and prints the misleading 'No artifacts.pkl; will try to reconstruct...'. Execution then reaches line 257 `pred_cnn, pred_tl = wg_fin.run_inference(...)`, which raises AttributeError and is re-raised by `raise`. The artifacts branch at line 289 makes the same call. The committed output at line 118 shows '[Errno 2] No such file or directory: training_artifacts/artifacts.pkl', which only a version of the library that had load_artifacts could print.

The notebook imports `financial_impact` before it puts the repo root on sys.path, and it hard-codes the author's own absolute path as repo_root. A fresh kernel, or any other machine, fails with ModuleNotFoundError or FileNotFoundError. Line 169 `from financial_impact import financial as wg_fin` runs before line 171 `repo_root = "/Users/<author>/Desktop/Capstone/waferguard-ml"` and the later `sys.path.insert(0, repo_root)`. Jupyter starts the kernel in wafer_images/, where `financial_impact` (a repo-root package) can't be found. pyproject.toml doesn't package it either: the project is named waferguard-ml and CI runs `poetry install --no-root`. Even if the import worked, data_path and models_dir are built from that literal user path, so `np.load(data_path)` fails anywhere else.

`compute_financials` accepts a `financial_params` argument but never uses it. A caller who passes site-specific costs silently gets figures computed from the built-in FINANCIAL_PARAMS. Lines 235-236 set `financial_params = FINANCIAL_PARAMS` when it is None, and the variable is never read again. Line 240 `params = get_params(binary_label)` and get_params/decompose (lines 188-199) look everything up in the module-level FINANCIAL_PARAMS.

`compute_financials` raises KeyError on an empty batch, so the `if not df_financial.empty` / `if not df_batch.empty` guards below it are dead and a zero-wafer batch crashes instead of returning a zero summary. `build_batch_df([], ...)` returns `pd.DataFrame([])`, which has no columns. In compute_financials the loop adds no rows, and line 273 `pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("priority_score", ...)` then raises KeyError 'priority_score' before lines 275-295 can apply their empty-frame fallbacks.

The summary's batch `avg_confidence` is the unweighted mean of per-pattern averages, not the mean over wafers, so a pattern with a handful of wafers counts as much as one with thousands and the reported batch confidence is wrong. Line 291 `round(float(df_batch["avg_confidence"].mean()) ...)` averages the per-pattern `avg_confidence` column that build_batch_df (line 175) computes once per unique label, and ignores `count`. The committed output shows a batch avg_confidence of 0.9806, although the top patterns each sit at 0.995 or higher.

`decode_labels` maps any class ID missing from `id_to_binary` to '00000000' (Normal: 'No action required — wafer passes electrical test'). An incomplete mapping therefore fails open and reports defective wafers as good, with zero loss. Line 151 `id_to_binary.get(int(cid), "00000000")`. The notebook's artifacts branch (line 291) passes `artifacts.get("id_to_binary", {})`, so an artifacts file without that key would decode every wafer as Normal. compute_financials would then report defective_wafers 0, total_daily_loss 0 and top_action 'None'. get_params (lines 197-198) also returns Normal params for any label it can't decompose.

The dollar costs, downtime rates and yield ranges in FINANCIAL_PARAMS, and the combo aggregation rules in get_params, are hard-coded business figures. Nothing in the repo shows a source or sign-off for them, yet they drive the ranked repair recommendations. Line 17 `# --- Financial mapping (copied from notebook)`, but the notebook added in this diff has no such table. get_params (lines 200-210) invents rules: repair costs are summed, downtime takes the max, yield is `ylos[0] + 0.5 * sum(ylos[1:])` capped at 1.0, and replacement cost skips None (Random). No spec, data file or comment traces any of these.

The diff changes .gitignore in ways the financial refactor doesn't need. It stops ignoring PresentationPDFs/ and architecture_report.pdf, starts ignoring requirements.txt, and ignores only one hard-coded LOT_001 JSON report, so reports for any other batch ID would show up as untracked files. The diff removes `PresentationPDFs/` and `architecture_report.pdf` and adds `requirements.txt` and `reports_LOT_001/refactor_demo/batch_summary_LOT_001.json`. save_reports writes `batch_summary_{batch_id}.json` under `reports_{BATCH_ID}/`, so only the LOT_001 path is covered.

The committed cell outputs carry the author's personal absolute paths and username, and they came from a different version of financial.py, so the report figures shown can't be reproduced from this code. Lines 116-122 and 162 contain '/Users/<author>/Desktop/Capstone/...'. Line 124 shows yield_range '18%–85%' with an en dash, while financial.py line 261 formats it with a hyphen: `f"{...}%-{...}%"`. The cell's execution_count is null, and its output includes a load_artifacts error that the current module can't produce.

The notebook's documentation contradicts the code: it names a `waferguard.financial` library that doesn't exist, and it promises a synthetic-demo fallback that isn't implemented. financial.py's docstring also lists a config key the function ignores. Line 102 says 'using the `waferguard.financial` library', but the package is `financial_impact.financial`. Line 167 says 'otherwise fall back to synthetic demo', but the cell has no synthetic path: it re-raises or calls `raise SystemExit`. financial.py line 233 lists CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD among the needed config keys, but compute_financials reads `config.get("low_conf_count", 0)` and never uses it.

The notebook hard-codes a 38-entry label mapping and rebuilds class IDs from it, duplicating the mapping app/labels.py already provides, so the two can drift apart. Lines 192-231 define `label_mapping` inline, and lines 232-235 derive pattern_to_id, id_to_pattern and id_to_binary by sorting. app/labels.py already defines ID_TO_PATTERN and PATTERN_TO_ID with the same ordering. `y_class_all` (line 247) is computed and never used.

save_reports builds file paths by inserting an unsanitised batch_id into an f-string. If the 'Streamlit-compatible' library is ever fed a user-supplied batch ID, a value containing '../' could write files outside outdir. Line 319 `csv_path = f"{outdir}/financial_report_{batch_id}.csv"`, and lines 320-321 do the same, with no validation of batch_id. The module docstring advertises the library as Streamlit-compatible.

The output column `evoa_30d` is named for a fixed 30-day horizon, but it is computed from the configurable PLANNING_HORIZON, so the column is mislabelled whenever the horizon is changed. Line 249 `avoided = daily_loss * planning_horizon`, where `planning_horizon = config.get("PLANNING_HORIZON", 30)` (line 245). Line 268 writes the result as `"evoa_30d"`.

build_batch_df rescans the whole label list once per unique label to collect confidences, doing O(wafers × patterns) Python work on the batch path where a single grouped pass would do. Line 168 `confs_this = [float(confidences[i]) for i, lbl in enumerate(binary_labels) if lbl == binary_label]` sits inside the loop over `pattern_counts`. For the notebook's 38,015-wafer batch with up to 38 labels, that is about 1.4M iterations.
